note: Which figure stands in for which thing the play scene draws today as a capsule. Keys are HostViews keys (Runtime/Play/HostViews.cs) and the people layer's job blocks (Editor/World/People/people.json). A list is a pool: pick by the person's id so the same person always looks the same. Capsules stay the fallback for any key not listed. 'patrol' is deliberately not listed: the patrol is a robot, Vela's PatrolRobot prefab (HostViews.cs, host.patrolRobot), and RoleFigure('patrol') returns null so no human figure is ever picked for it; the 'security' figure is the posted and response officer (security/*, unit/*, hostile officers), brief 063. Brief 067 (W1): the rivals are the Velvet Set: `rival`, `rival_b` and `rival_c` are three colourways of one look on Commuter D4's body, `rival_d` the crew's woman on Commuter C6's (the hood is her silhouette); pool `role/rival`; rival-1..5 take them rival, rival_b, rival_d, rival_c, rival (playViews).

playViews.body/<key>: the same figure as the person, playing `lying` (or laid flat as the capsule is); `carried` over the carrier's shoulder

lodScreen.note: LODGroup transition heights as a fraction of screen height, a start for Latch to tune. A 1.75 m figure is 53 px of 1080 (0.049) at play zoom (ortho 14, pitch 38), so play zoom lands on the last LOD of each figure; the follow view and close views land on LOD0.

Not measured here: GPU time. Triangle counts at play zoom are the last LOD of each figure (1.5k cell and cast, about 1.5k crowd): 100 figures on screen is about 150k triangles and 100 skinned renderers, so the cost to watch is skinning and animator updates, not triangles. Redline's 4.5 ms is for Latch to measure on the Air with the real scene.
The contact sheets are from a scratch Unity project (built-in Standard shader, one sun, no grade, no shadows). The look in the game's URP scene with Glint's grade will differ.

forLatch: 1. Get the files: `bun tools/figures/run.ts` builds out/people-models/People (needs Blender and the store); `--install` mirrors it to unity/Assets/Suborned/People. Git-ignore that folder like Kit/ (97 MB). Splice may want a hash-checked copy step like the kit's.

2. Everything is imported by its .meta: figures as Humanoid with an avatar from the model, textures with the right colour space, materials bound by name (URP Lit), clips Humanoid with loops set. Checked in Unity 6000.6.2f1 with URP 17.6: avatars valid, LOD groups made, materials resolve.

3. Per figure build a prefab: the FBX root (LODGroup from the names; set the transition heights from `lodScreenHeights`), an Animator with the FBX's avatar and one shared AnimatorController, a CapsuleCollider (1.75 m, radius 0.4) for clicks (the models carry none), Apply Root Motion off. The figure faces +Z; turn the object to the heading the capsule faces.

5. Mapping from the play scene: `playRoles`, `families` and `jobBlocks` in the manifest. Pick from a pool by the person's id so the same person always looks the same. Keys with no entry keep their capsule.

6. The family tints in HostViews (café peach, office teal, guard, driver) are no longer needed: the figures carry their own colours. The signals (cones, rings, price chips, fight tracers) stay as they are.

4. One AnimatorController for all (FigureBuild already makes it). Cross-fade with `CrossFadeInFixedTime(state, 0.15f)`, not `CrossFade(state, 0.15f)`: the second is a fraction of the clip, and an idle of 8.8 s blends for 1.3 s (the Scout's hands stayed on her hips after she stopped). The fourth argument of CrossFade is seconds, not a 0..1 phase.
5. Mapping from the play scene: `playRoles`, `families` and `jobBlocks` in the manifest.

6. Stride: `naturalSpeedMs` per locomotion clip was re-measured in Unity (walk 1.29, walk_f 0.99, run 2.52, walk_armed 2.44, run_armed 3.11 m/s). `walk_armed` and `run_armed` are fast clips: below about 2 m/s play `walk` (or `walk_f`) and keep the weapon in the aim pose, or the armed walk plays at 0.6x in slow motion.

7. Carried and lying (updated 2026-10-18, Forma). CARRY: the carried person plays `carried_drape` (never `carried`, a flat bar from above) and the carrier plays `carry_shoulder` (moving; stride from naturalSpeedMs 1.29, same legs as `walk`) or `carry_shoulder_idle` (standing). Seat: turn the carried figure to the carrier's heading + 180 degrees (its trunk hangs down his back, its legs down his chest), then move it so its Hips bone is at the carrier's RightShoulder bone + 0.10 m along the carrier's right + 0.10 m up (+ 0 along his heading); recompute each frame from the bone, as now. In code: `figure.model.rotation = Quaternion.Euler(0, carrierYaw + 180f, 0); var want = rShoulder.position + carrierRight * 0.10f + Vector3.up * 0.10f; model.position += want - hips.position;` (tools/figures/scratch/FigCarry.cs does exactly this: mode new, seat 0.10,0.10,0, yawadd 180). Cross-fade into both clips as usual (CrossFadeInFixedTime 0.15). The Enforcer's carrying hand now closes round the legs (two-bone solve to the carried knees, fingers curled), standing and walking. Nobody runs carrying Vale, so there is no carry run. LYING: `lying` and the knockout and kill clips end on the ground: place the figure at the body's point (no lift). The old `carried` clip (limp, flat) is a lying pose: use it only for a body laid across something.
8. Standing, walking and running clips now put the soles on the ground themselves (Root Transform Position (Y): Based Upon Feet; the lying, falling and carried clips keep the original height).

9. Materials are matte now (metallic 0, smoothness 0.15 on the no-map materials; the mapped ones rebaked to the world's cloth). If a figure is still too bright, change `_Smoothness` on its material, not the map.

10. Serving tray (brief 022, Forma, 2026-10-18). Inez is figure `waitress`; the other café staff are cafe_w2/w3/w5. New clips `serve` (standing: right hand holds a tray out at waist height, palm up; the left arm as the idle has it, 8.8 s loop) and `serve_walk` (the same right arm over the women's walk, natural speed 0.99 like walk_f; use it on the way to and from a table if you want the tray carried both ways). Play `serve` in the `serving` phase instead of `talk`. The prop is People/Props/tray/tray.fbx (cream enamel dish, chrome rim, one thin brass line, cup, saucer, coffee, spoon; 2.2k tris; URP Lit materials tray_cream/chrome/brass/coffee beside it; origin = the middle of the tray's underside; root rotation identity). Attach: `var hand = anim.GetBoneTransform(HumanBodyBones.RightHand); prop.SetParent(hand, false); prop.localPosition = ...; prop.localRotation = Quaternion.Euler(...)`, with the per-figure values in manifest.props[0].attach.perFigure (waitress: position (0.0114, 0.0475, -0.0442), euler (280.4, 98.1, 258.4); cafe_w2 and cafe_w3: (0.0001, 0.0450, -0.0481), (277.7, 215.0, 139.9); cafe_w5: (0.0170, 0.0463, -0.0438), (282.5, 96.6, 254.7)). They differ because each rig's hand bone has its own local axes. SetActive(true) only while the state is `serve` or `serve_walk`, false in every other state (it is one instance per figure, made when the figure is made). The tray is 0.32 m across, a hair over life so it reads at play zoom.

12. Seated customers (brief 022, Forma, 2026-10-19). Clips `sit` (4.3 s loop), `sit_alt` (7 s loop, a second idle so a table does not breathe in step), `sit_talk` (44 s loop, hand gestures), `stand_to_sit` and `sit_to_stand` (2.3 s each, once). All play on every Humanoid figure, women and men alike, with Apply Root Motion off. PLACEMENT: put the figure's root (the object origin, at its feet) on the chair's `at` point at ground level, the figure turned to face the table pivot, and add nothing: the clips already put the pelvis over the root (hips 0.04 m behind the chair centre, 0.65 m up) and the feet on the floor for every pooled commuter. For the figures with their own rig (scout, tech, enforcer, guard, security, cafe_w5; waitress and cafe_w2/w3 are within 5 mm) add manifest.seat.perFigure[id].rootUp / rootForward (about -0.03 m up). The chair is the café set's Tulip chair (seat bowl 0.462 m, cushion top 0.474 m; manifest.seat.chair). Chain: play stand_to_sit when the person arrives at the seat, CrossFadeInFixedTime(sit, 0.15f) at its end; sit_to_stand when they leave, then idle or walk (the figure stands over the seat, inside the chair: step it off in the same frame). Pick sit, sit_alt or sit_talk by the person's id hash; sit_talk while talking. Loop flags are set in the .meta. Checked in Unity on the real chair with 18 figures (briefs/022/forma/seated-before-after.png, seated-chair-contract.png); see manifest.seat.knownGaps.

13. Carry hip tear (brief 022, Forma, 2026-10-19). Fixed in the councillor's weights and mesh, not in the pose: nearest-surface skinning had given the jacket hem and waist band the forearm's and upper arm's influence, so a body hung over a shoulder dragged those vertices a metre from their neighbours (edges stretched 58 times). The arms' weights are now taken off the waist and hips on every figure (figlib.torso_guard; standing, walking, running and aiming checked unchanged on 18 figures), and the councillor also has the thin strip of faces that joined his sleeve to his jacket side cut (figures.json torsoWebs; on the puffy-jacket figures it opens a hole when the arms move, so it is off for them). The edges still stretched past 5x went from 138 to 32 (ragged hem corners remain at the side: briefs/022/forma/carry-hip-before-after.png). Install and the councillor needs no code change. If another body (a guard, a passer) shows a sliver when carried, set "torsoWebs": true on its figures.json entry and rebuild.
